(1) `no-refusal` is a question NEVER PUT, and the probe says so in its own detail: "the refusal was never provoked". It was not in NOT_ASKED, so 94 non-measurements scored as refutations. It is a THIRD category and is kept out of NOT_ASKED deliberately: not "the harness could not set it up" (ours to fix), not "the host would not answer" (a fact about the host), but "the precondition did not occur" — a CONDITIONAL probe, whose question exists only when the host misbehaves. Round 102 taught exactly this from the trace side and the lesson did not carry: a claim is only as good as the set of strings the thing it watches can produce. Claims now match the answer KEY — an enum the probe picks — as well as the prose a later commit can reword.  AND THE READING WAS n=1. `roundToJudgeOn` handed the judge the newest round, so a probe that fires 18% of the time was 82% likely to be judged on a round carrying no measurement at all. triage.mjs argues at length that one round is a fact about the code AND the host's mood that afternoon; the prediction ledger was the one reader ignoring it. Predictions are now judged across every eligible round and report the split — held / FAILED / never put — with BOTH as its own verdict when the decided rounds disagree, because a population that contradicts itself is a finding about the host, not a tie to be broken quietly.  SIBLING SWEEP: all 38 probe ids, every distinct answer value across 133 rounds. Only `no-refusal` qualifies. `no-group-id` ("the host would not name the group it just made"), `no-id` ("the fresh shape would not report an id"), `none` and `unreadable` are the host DECLINING a question that WAS put — a finding, not a starved probe — and they stay where they are.
